decisions.choice: Deborah sang, and Barak with her: she leads the song
alternatives: Deborah and Barak sang together as equals
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and feminine, agreeing with Deborah, who is named first; Barak joins her. Exodus 15:1 has a singular verb with Moses in the same way, though the people sing with him.

decisions.choice: on that day: the day of the victory over Sisera told in chapter 4
decisions.reason: The song that follows (verses 2-31a) is a poem that retells the same battle. It celebrates what chapter 4 narrates, and adds details the story does not give, such as the storm (verses 4, 20-21) and the tribes that stayed away (verses 15-17).

decisions.choice: sang this song:
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces the words that follow. Balanced and Readable name them as a song.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of Judges 5.
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns for God are written plainly.

decisions.choice: "пела Девора и Варак", the verb in the singular
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is feminine singular: Deborah sings and Barak with her (m1). Literal keeps the singular verb before the two names, as Russian allows; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

decisions.choice: the song keeps the English poetry lines (\q) and stands inside one pair of «», with “ ” for the speeches within it
decisions.reason: The song of Deborah is laid out as verse at every level, as the English has it.

decisions.choice: the song set in short lines at every level, with the Hebrew's line breaks; Deborah says "aku"; the LORD is addressed as "Engkau" in a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Poetry as the style guide sets (section 12): the singer speaks as "aku", as the psalmist does, and speaks to God with the capitalised pronouns.

decisions.choice: "umawit si Debora at si Barak"
decisions.reason: She leads the song, and Barak with her (m1).

decisions.choice: "nang araw na iyon"
decisions.reason: The day of the victory over Sisera told in chapter 4 (m2).

records.literal_gloss: In letting loose of locks in Israel, in offering themselves willingly of [the] people, bless Yahweh!

en.L: "When locks hung loose in Israel, \q when [the] people offered themselves willingly, \q bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.B: "When long hair hung loose in Israel, \q when the people volunteered freely, \q bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: "In Israel the fighters let their hair hang long, \q and the people gladly offered themselves for battle. \q Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

sw.L: "Nywele zilipoachwa ndefu katika Israeli, \q watu walipojitoa kwa hiari, \q mhimidini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.B: "Nywele ndefu zilipoachwa wazi katika Israeli, \q watu walipojitolea kwa hiari, \q mhimidini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.R: "Katika Israeli wapiganaji waliziacha nywele zao ziwe ndefu, \q na watu walijitolea kwa furaha kwenda vitani. \q Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!

es.L: «Cuando se soltaron las cabelleras en Israel, \q cuando [el] pueblo se ofreció voluntariamente, \q ¡{{plural_you:bendigan|bendecid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!
es.B: «Cuando en Israel se dejaron sueltas las largas cabelleras, \q cuando el pueblo se ofreció de buena gana, \q ¡{{plural_you:bendigan|bendecid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!
es.R: «En Israel los guerreros se dejaron crecer el cabello, \q y el pueblo se ofreció con gusto para la batalla. \q ¡{{plural_you:Alaben|Alabad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!

fr.L: « Quand les chevelures flottaient en Israël, \q quand [le] peuple s’offrait de plein gré, \q bénissez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !
fr.B: « Quand les longues chevelures flottaient en Israël, \q quand le peuple s’engageait librement, \q bénissez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !
fr.R: « En Israël, les combattants laissaient pousser leurs cheveux, \q et le peuple s’est offert de bon cœur pour la bataille. \q Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !

vi.L: "Khi tóc xõa dài trong Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q khi dân chúng tự nguyện dâng mình, \q hãy chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!
vi.B: "Khi các chiến sĩ Y-sơ-ra-ên để tóc xõa dài, \q khi dân chúng tự nguyện ra đi, \q hãy chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!
vi.R: "Trong Y-sơ-ra-ên, các chiến sĩ để tóc dài, \q và dân chúng vui lòng dâng mình ra trận. \q Hãy ca ngợi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!

ko.L: "이스라엘에서 머리털을 길게 풀어 늘어뜨렸을 때, \q 백성이 스스로 기꺼이 나섰을 때, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!
ko.B: "이스라엘에서 용사들이 긴 머리를 풀어 늘어뜨리고, \q 백성이 기꺼이 자원하여 나섰으니, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!
ko.R: "이스라엘의 용사들이 머리를 길게 늘어뜨리고, \q 백성이 기쁘게 싸움터로 나섰다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!

pt.L: "Quando as cabeleiras se soltaram em Israel, \q quando o povo se ofereceu de boa vontade, \q bendigam {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!
pt.B: "Quando os cabelos longos se soltaram em Israel, \q quando o povo se apresentou como voluntário, \q bendigam {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!
pt.R: "Em Israel os guerreiros deixaram o cabelo crescer, \q e o povo se ofereceu com alegria para a batalha. \q Louvem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!

am.L: «በእስራኤል የራስ ጠጉር በተለቀቀ ጊዜ፣ \q ሕዝቡ ራሳቸውን በፈቃዳቸው ባቀረቡ ጊዜ፣ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ባርኩ!
am.B: «በእስራኤል ረጅም ጠጉር በተለቀቀ ጊዜ፣ \q ሕዝቡ በገዛ ፈቃዳቸው በተነሡ ጊዜ፣ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ባርኩ!
am.R: «በእስራኤል ተዋጊዎቹ ጠጉራቸውን አሳደጉ፤ \q ሕዝቡም ለጦርነት በደስታ ራሳቸውን አቀረቡ። \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} አመስግኑ!

hi.L: "जब इस्राएल में लटें खुली लटकीं, \q जब लोगों ने अपनी इच्छा से अपने आप को अर्पित किया, \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को धन्य कहो!
hi.B: "जब इस्राएल में लंबे बाल खुले लहराए, \q जब लोग अपनी इच्छा से आगे आए, \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को धन्य कहो!
hi.R: "इस्राएल में योद्धाओं ने अपने बाल लंबे छोड़ दिए, \q और लोग ख़ुशी से लड़ाई के लिए आगे आए। \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की स्तुति करो!

ru.L: «Когда распустились кудри в Израиле, \q когда добровольно вызвался народ, — \q благословите {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}!
ru.B: «Когда в Израиле воины распустили волосы, \q когда народ по доброй воле пошёл в бой, — \q благословите {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}!
ru.R: «В Израиле воины не стригли волос, \q и народ охотно пошёл на битву. \q Хвалите {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}!

ja.L: 「イスラエルで髪が長く垂らされたとき、 \q 民が自ら進んで身をささげたとき、 \q {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}をほめたたえよ。
ja.B: 「イスラエルで戦士たちが長い髪を垂らしたとき、 \q 民が進んで志願したとき、 \q {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}をほめたたえよ。
ja.R: 「イスラエルでは、戦う者たちが髪を長く伸ばした。 \q 民は喜んで戦いに身をささげた。 \q {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}を賛美しなさい。

uk.L: «Коли розпускали коси в Ізраїлі, \q коли народ охоче віддавав себе, \q благословіть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}!
uk.B: «Коли довге волосся вільно спадало в Ізраїлі, \q коли народ зголошувався охоче, \q благословіть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}!
uk.R: «В Ізраїлі воїни відпустили довге волосся, \q і народ радо віддав себе на битву. \q Хваліть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}!

id.L: "Ketika rambut terurai panjang di Israel, \q ketika bangsa itu merelakan diri, \q pujilah {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}!
id.B: "Ketika para pejuang di Israel membiarkan rambutnya terurai, \q ketika bangsa itu dengan rela menyerahkan diri, \q pujilah {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}!
id.R: "Di Israel para pejuang membiarkan rambutnya tumbuh panjang, \q dan bangsa itu dengan senang hati maju berperang. \q Pujilah {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}!

zh.L: “当以色列中头发披散的时候， \q 当百姓甘心献上自己的时候， \q 你们要称颂{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}！
zh.B: “当以色列人长发飘垂， \q 当百姓甘心踊跃从军， \q 你们要称颂{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}！
zh.R: “在以色列，战士们留着长发， \q 百姓也乐意献身作战。 \q 你们要赞美{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}！

pa.L: "ਜਦੋਂ ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੇਸ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਲਮਕਦੇ ਸਨ, \q ਜਦੋਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੀ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਨੂੰ ਅਰਪਣ ਕੀਤਾ, \q {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਨੂੰ ਧੰਨ ਆਖੋ!
pa.B: "ਜਦੋਂ ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੰਮੇ ਕੇਸ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਛੱਡੇ ਗਏ, \q ਜਦੋਂ ਲੋਕ ਆਪ ਮੁਹਾਰੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਆਏ, \q ਤਾਂ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਨੂੰ ਧੰਨ ਆਖੋ!
pa.R: "ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੋਧਿਆਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਕੇਸ ਲੰਮੇ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਛੱਡ ਦਿੱਤੇ, \q ਅਤੇ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੇ ਚਾਅ ਨਾਲ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਨੂੰ ਲੜਾਈ ਲਈ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤਾ। \q {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਕਰੋ!

tl.L: "Nang ilugay ang mga buhok sa Israel, \q nang kusang-loob na ihandog ng bayan ang kanilang sarili, \q purihin {{divine_name:ang PANGINOON|si Yahweh}}!
tl.B: "Nang ilugay ang mahahabang buhok sa Israel, \q nang kusang-loob na magboluntaryo ang bayan, \q purihin {{divine_name:ang PANGINOON|si Yahweh}}!
tl.R: "Sa Israel ay hinayaan ng mga mandirigma na humaba ang kanilang buhok, \q at buong-galak na inihandog ng bayan ang kanilang sarili sa labanan. \q Purihin {{divine_name:ang PANGINOON|si Yahweh}}!

decisions.choice: when locks of hair hung loose: the warriors left their hair uncut, a sign that they had given themselves to fight the LORD's war
alternatives: when the leaders took the lead in Israel
decisions.reason: The verb means "let loose" or "let go", and the noun is used for long uncut hair in Numbers 6:5 (the Nazirite's hair) and Deuteronomy 32:42 (the long-haired heads of the enemy). The other reading takes both words from a root found in related languages that means "be first" or "lead": "when the leaders took the lead in Israel". That would match the commanders of verse 9. The evidence is divided.

decisions.choice: offered themselves willingly: came forward to fight of their own free will
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for freewill offerings (Exodus 35:29); here people give themselves. It returns in verse 9. Not every tribe came forward (verses 15-17).

decisions.choice: the two "when" clauses give the reason for praise; "bless the LORD" is a command to the hearers
decisions.reason: The command is plural. The song opens and returns (verse 9) with this call to praise the LORD for the people's readiness to fight.

decisions.choice: a double quotation mark opens here and closes at the end of the song in verse 31, before "And the land had peace"
decisions.reason: Verse 1 introduces the song as the words Deborah and Barak sang, so the whole poem is set as one quotation. Words quoted inside it (verses 23, 28, 30) take single quotes.

decisions.choice: fighters (Readable); for battle (Readable); praise (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says who let their hair hang loose and why the people offered themselves, as verses 8-9 and 13-18 make clear. Blessing God means praising him, so Readable says "praise".

decisions.choice: "mhimidini BWANA" (L, B) and "msifuni BWANA" (R) for "bless the LORD"; the song is set inside double quotation marks from here to verse 31, as in the English
decisions.reason: "Kumhimidi" is the Swahili verb for blessing God in praise; "kumbariki" would suggest giving a blessing to him. Readable uses the everyday "kusifu" (praise), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the song is set in lines and opened with «, which closes at the end of verse 31 before "Y la tierra tuvo reposo"; speeches inside it take “ ”
alternatives: lines and quotation marks placed as in the English
decisions.reason: As the English does, the Song of Deborah is set in lines at every level, with the breaks placed at Spanish phrase boundaries. Spanish narrative quotation marks («») open the song here and close at the end of verse 31; the angel's curse (verse 23) and the words of Sisera's mother (verses 28-30) take the inner marks “ ”.

decisions.choice: the song is set in lines at every level, as the English is, within French quotation marks that open here and close at the end of verse 31, before "Et le pays fut en repos"; words quoted inside the song take “ ” (verses 23, 28, 30)
alternatives: no quotation marks around the song
decisions.reason: For Judges 5: the song is poetry and every record of it is set in lines, placed at French phrase boundaries. The narrator introduces it in verse 1 ("en disant") and closes the chapter after it, so it is quoted like a speech, as the English does; the French style guide uses « » outside and “ ” inside.

decisions.choice: "quand les chevelures flottaient" (L); "quand les longues chevelures flottaient" (B)
alternatives: "quand les chefs se mirent à la tête" (the other reading of the Hebrew verb)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the rare Hebrew words as hair left loose and uncut, the sign of warriors given to the LORD's war. French "chevelure" keeps that picture without saying more than the Hebrew; Readable says what it meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the song is set in lines (\q) at every level, as the English is, and its double quotation mark opens here and closes in verse 31
decisions.reason: The Song of Deborah is poetry, set in lines as the terms note says; Vietnamese places its own breaks at its phrase boundaries, following the Hebrew cola.

decisions.choice: "hãy chúc tụng CHÚA" (L, B); "hãy ca ngợi CHÚA" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese Psalms (103:1): "chúc tụng" for blessing the LORD, the plainer "ca ngợi" (praise) at Readable.

decisions.choice: the song is set in lines as the English is, with Korean breaks at Korean phrase boundaries; one double quotation mark opens here and closes in verse 31
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for Judges 5. The singer speaks to God in the formal polite style (합쇼체), as the psalmist does, and calls on kings and peoples in the plain style; the narrating lines use the plain written style with the honorific for God.

decisions.choice: the song as one quotation, opened here and closed in verse 31; each level's line breaks as in the English
decisions.reason: The Song of Deborah is poetry: every level keeps its lines where the English level has them, and the whole song is one quotation, as the English sets it (r-en-1), with the quoted words inside it (verses 23, 28, 30) in single quotation marks. The Portuguese is drafted from the Hebrew and its gloss, line by line, in its own words. "Bendigam" (L, B) is plural, a call to the hearers (m3); Readable says "Louvem", as the English says "Praise".

decisions.choice: as cabeleiras se soltaram (L); os cabelos longos se soltaram (B)
decisions.reason: The line follows the reading of m1, the long hair of men given to the LORD's war; "cabeleira" is the word for a full head of long hair.

decisions.choice: The song opens with "«" here and closes with "»" in verse 31, before the narrator's "the land had peace"; the quotations inside it (verses 23, 28, 30) are in "“ ”". Each level keeps the English level's line breaks, with the Amharic order inside each line.
alternatives: no quotation marks for the song
decisions.reason: So that the song has the same quotation structure as the English and the reader sets it in the same lines; Amharic places the verb at the end of each line, so a line holds the same content as the English line in Amharic order.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को धन्य कहो" (L, B); "की स्तुति करो" (R)
decisions.reason: To bless the LORD is to praise him; Hindi "आशीष देना" is said of a greater to a lesser, so Literal and Balanced say "धन्य कहो" (call him blessed), and Readable "स्तुति करो" (praise), as the English Readable does. The song is set in lines (\q) where the English has them, and stands inside one double quotation mark from verse 2 to verse 31.

decisions.choice: The song set in lines with \q where the English level has them, one pair of guillemets from verse 2 to verse 31, “ ” for the words quoted inside it (verses 23, 28, 30)
decisions.reason: As Russian style 7a sets for poetry: the lines follow the English level's breaks. The whole song is one quotation, as in English, so it opens here and closes in verse 31 before the narrator's last sentence.

decisions.choice: "распустились кудри" (L); "воины распустили волосы" (B); "воины не стригли волос" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is read as hair hanging loose, the uncut hair of men who had given themselves to the LORD's war (m1). Literal keeps the image; Balanced names the warriors; Readable says what was done, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The song (5:2-31) is one quotation, opened here with "「" and closed in 5:31 before the narrator's last line; quotations inside it take "『 』". It is in the plain style at every level, Readable too, set in the English lines (\q); God's acts keep the light respect forms and God is addressed as "あなた" and "主よ"; calls to praise "ほめたたえよ" (L, B), "賛美しなさい" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Song of Moses in Exodus 15 in Japanese; a song keeps its plain imperatives (Numbers consistency notes).

decisions.choice: "when locks hung loose": "髪が長く垂らされたとき" (L), "戦士たちが長い髪を垂らしたとき" (B), "戦う者たちが髪を長く伸ばした" (R)
alternatives: "指導者たちが先頭に立ったとき"
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1 (uncertain): warriors with uncut hair, given to the LORD's war; the other reading is in the footnote.

decisions.choice: "rambut terurai" (L, B), "rambutnya tumbuh panjang" (R); "pujilah TUHAN" for "bless the LORD"
decisions.reason: The warriors' uncut hair (m1) is kept as an image; "memuji" says blessing God in plain Indonesian, as "memberkati" is used of God blessing people.

decisions.choice: the song as one quotation, opened here and closed in verse 31; its lines as the English \q lines
decisions.reason: As the English: the whole poem is the words Deborah and Barak sang, so one “ opens here and ” closes before the narrator's last line in verse 31; words quoted inside it (verses 23, 28, 30) take ‘ ’. Each level has the English level's lines, broken at Chinese phrase boundaries, drafted from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "称颂上主" (L, B); "赞美上主" (R)
decisions.reason: The glossary's 称颂 for blessing God; Readable says praise, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਧੰਨ ਆਖੋ (L, B); ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਕਰੋ (R)
decisions.reason: Barekhu, said again in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "Nang ilugay ang mga buhok"
decisions.reason: The warriors left their hair uncut, a sign that they had given themselves to fight the LORD's war (m1).

decisions.choice: "kusang-loob na ihandog ... ang kanilang sarili"
decisions.reason: Came forward to fight of their own free will (m2).

decisions.choice: "Nang ... nang ... purihin"
decisions.reason: The two "when" clauses give the reason for praise; "purihin" is a command to the hearers (m3).

source.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ מְלָכִ֔ים הַאֲזִ֖ינוּ רֹֽזְנִ֑ים אָֽנֹכִ֗י לַֽיהוָה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָשִׁ֔ירָה אֲזַמֵּ֕ר לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, kings; give ear, rulers; I to Yahweh, I will sing; I will make music to Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.

en.L: Hear, kings; give ear, rulers! \q I, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I will sing; \q I will make music to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.B: Listen, you kings; pay attention, you rulers! \q I will sing, I myself, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q I will make music to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: Listen, kings! Pay attention, rulers! \q I will sing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I will make music for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

sw.L: Sikieni, enyi wafalme; tegeni sikio, enyi watawala! \q Mimi, kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mimi nitaimba; \q nitamwimbia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, zaburi.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, enyi wafalme; tegeni masikio, enyi watawala! \q Nitaimba, mimi mwenyewe, kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q nitamwimbia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, nyimbo za sifa.
sw.R: Sikilizeni, wafalme! Tegeni masikio, watawala! \q Nitamwimbia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Nitampigia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, muziki.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}}, reyes; {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}, gobernantes! \q Yo, {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, yo cantaré; \q cantaré salmos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, reyes; {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención, gobernantes! \q Yo misma cantaré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, \q cantaré salmos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, reyes! ¡{{plural_you:Presten|Prestad}} atención, gobernantes! \q Voy a cantar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Voy a cantar salmos {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.

fr.L: Écoutez, rois ; prêtez l’oreille, princes ! \q Moi, c’est {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} que je chanterai, moi ; \q je jouerai pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.B: Écoutez, rois ; soyez attentifs, princes ! \q Je chanterai, oui, moi, je chanterai {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} ; \q je célébrerai {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, par la musique.
fr.R: Écoutez, rois ! Faites attention, princes ! \q Je vais chanter pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Je vais jouer de la musique pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.

vi.L: Hỡi các vua, hãy nghe; hỡi các quân vương, hãy lắng tai! \q Tôi, tôi sẽ hát cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q tôi sẽ đàn ca cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Hỡi các vua, hãy lắng nghe; hỡi các quân vương, hãy chú ý! \q Chính tôi sẽ hát cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q tôi sẽ đàn ca chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Hỡi các vua, hãy nghe! Hỡi các quân vương, hãy chú ý! \q Tôi sẽ hát cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Tôi sẽ đàn ca cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 들어라, 왕들아. 귀를 기울여라, 통치자들아. \q 나는, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께, 나는 노래하리라. \q 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 찬송하리라.
ko.B: 왕들아, 들어라! 통치자들아, 귀를 기울여라! \q 나는, 바로 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 노래하리라. \q 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 찬송하리라.
ko.R: 왕들아, 들어라! 통치자들아, 귀를 기울여라! \q 나는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 노래하겠다. \q 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 찬송을 부르겠다.

pt.L: Ouçam, reis; deem ouvidos, governantes! \q Eu, {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, eu cantarei; \q cantarei louvores {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.B: Escutem, ó reis; prestem atenção, ó governantes! \q Eu mesma cantarei {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}; \q cantarei louvores com música {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.R: Escutem, reis! Prestem atenção, governantes! \q Eu vou cantar {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. \q Vou cantar louvores com música para {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.

am.L: ነገሥታት ሆይ፣ ስሙ፤ ገዢዎች ሆይ፣ አድምጡ! \q እኔ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}}፣ እኔ እዘምራለሁ፤ \q ለእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} እቀኛለሁ።
am.B: እናንተ ነገሥታት፣ ስሙ፤ እናንተ ገዢዎች፣ አድምጡ! \q እኔ ራሴ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} እዘምራለሁ፤ \q ለእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} እቀኛለሁ።
am.R: ነገሥታት ሆይ፣ ስሙ! ገዢዎች ሆይ፣ አድምጡ! \q {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} እዘምራለሁ። \q ለእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:ለእግዚአብሔር|ለያህዌ}} በዝማሬ ምስጋና አቀርባለሁ።

hi.L: हे राजाओ, सुनो; हे शासको, कान लगाओ! \q मैं, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के लिए मैं गाऊँगी; \q मैं {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर का भजन गाऊँगी।
hi.B: हे राजाओ, सुनो; हे शासको, ध्यान दो! \q मैं, हाँ मैं, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के लिए गाऊँगी; \q मैं {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर का भजन गाऊँगी।
hi.R: हे राजाओ, सुनो! हे शासको, ध्यान दो! \q मैं {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के लिए गीत गाऊँगी। \q मैं {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर के लिए संगीत बजाऊँगी।

ru.L: Слушайте, цари; внимайте, правители! \q Я — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, я буду петь, \q буду играть {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, Богу Израиля.
ru.B: Слушайте, цари, внимайте, правители! \q Это я буду петь {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, \q буду славить музыкой {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, Бога Израиля.
ru.R: Слушайте, цари! Внимайте, правители! \q Я буду петь {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}. \q Я буду играть музыку для {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, Бога Израиля.

ja.L: 王たちよ、聞きなさい。君主たちよ、耳を傾けなさい。 \q わたしは、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}に、このわたしは歌おう。 \q イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}に、わたしはほめ歌を奏でよう。
ja.B: 王たちよ、聞きなさい。君主たちよ、耳を傾けなさい。 \q わたしは歌う。このわたしが{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}に向かって歌う。 \q イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}に向かって、わたしはほめ歌を奏でる。
ja.R: 王たちよ、聞きなさい。支配者たちよ、よく聞きなさい。 \q わたしは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}に向かって歌う。 \q イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}のために、わたしは歌を奏でる。

uk.L: Слухайте, царі; наставте вухо, володарі! \q Я, {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЕВІ|Ягве}}, я співатиму; \q я гратиму {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЕВІ|Ягве}}, Богові Ізраїля.
uk.B: Слухайте, царі; зважайте, володарі! \q Я співатиму, саме я, {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЕВІ|Ягве}}; \q я гратиму {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЕВІ|Ягве}}, Богові Ізраїля.
uk.R: Слухайте, царі! Зважайте, володарі! \q Я співатиму {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЕВІ|Ягве}}. \q Я гратиму для {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, Бога Ізраїля.

id.L: Dengarlah, hai raja-raja; pasanglah telinga, hai para penguasa! \q Aku, bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, aku akan bernyanyi; \q aku akan bermazmur bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, Allah Israel.
id.B: Dengarlah, hai raja-raja! Perhatikanlah, hai para penguasa! \q Aku akan bernyanyi bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, \q aku akan bermazmur bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, Allah Israel.
id.R: Dengarlah, hai raja-raja! Perhatikanlah, hai para penguasa! \q Aku akan bernyanyi bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}. \q Aku akan memainkan musik bagi {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, Allah Israel.

zh.L: 众王啊，要听；君主们啊，要侧耳！ \q 我，我要向{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}歌唱； \q 我要向{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}奏乐歌颂。
zh.B: 君王们，你们要听；统治者们，你们要留心听！ \q 我要歌唱，我要亲自向{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}歌唱； \q 我要向{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}弹奏歌颂。
zh.R: 君王们，听啊！统治者们，留心听啊！ \q 我要向{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}歌唱。 \q 我要为{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}奏乐。

pa.L: ਹੇ ਰਾਜਿਓ, ਸੁਣੋ; ਹੇ ਹਾਕਮੋ, ਕੰਨ ਲਾਓ! \q ਮੈਂ, {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਲਈ, ਮੈਂ ਗਾਵਾਂਗੀ; \q ਮੈਂ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}}, ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ, ਲਈ ਰਾਗ ਛੇੜਾਂਗੀ।
pa.B: ਹੇ ਰਾਜਿਓ, ਸੁਣੋ; ਹੇ ਹਾਕਮੋ, ਧਿਆਨ ਦਿਓ! \q ਮੈਂ ਗਾਵਾਂਗੀ, ਮੈਂ ਆਪ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਲਈ ਗਾਵਾਂਗੀ; \q ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਲਈ ਮੈਂ ਸਾਜ਼ ਵਜਾਵਾਂਗੀ।
pa.R: ਰਾਜਿਓ, ਸੁਣੋ! ਹਾਕਮੋ, ਧਿਆਨ ਕਰੋ! \q ਮੈਂ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਦੇ ਗੀਤ ਗਾਵਾਂਗੀ। \q ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਲਈ ਮੈਂ ਸੰਗੀਤ ਛੇੜਾਂਗੀ।

tl.L: Makinig kayo, mga hari; duminig kayo, mga pinuno! \q Ako, {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}, ako ay aawit; \q aawit ako ng papuri {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}, ang Diyos ng Israel.
tl.B: Makinig kayo, mga hari; pakinggan ninyo, mga pinuno! \q Aawit ako, ako mismo, {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}; \q aawit ako ng papuri {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}, ang Diyos ng Israel.
tl.R: Makinig kayo, mga hari! Pakinggan ninyo, mga pinuno! \q Aawit ako {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}. \q Tutugtog at aawit ako {{divine_name:sa PANGINOON|kay Yahweh}}, ang Diyos ng Israel.

decisions.choice: kings and rulers: the rulers of the nations, called to hear what Israel's God has done
decisions.reason: Foreign kings are summoned as witnesses, as the kings of Canaan were defeated (verse 19). The same pair of words appears in Psalm 2:2 and Proverbs 8:15.

decisions.choice: I, I: the singer says "I" twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The pronoun is not needed with the verb, so repeating it stresses that the singer herself will praise the LORD, not the kings.

decisions.choice: make music: sing praise, often with instruments
decisions.reason: The verb is used for playing an instrument as well as singing praise (Psalm 33:2; 98:5).

decisions.choice: Eu mesma
decisions.reason: Portuguese marks the singer's gender where the English "I myself" does not: verse 1 has a feminine verb for Deborah, who leads the song (m1 there), and verse 7 has her say "I, Deborah", so Balanced says "eu mesma".

decisions.choice: feminine "गाऊँगी" for the singer's "I"
decisions.reason: Hindi verbs show the speaker's gender, which English does not. Verse 1 says Deborah sang, Barak with her, and verse 7 the singer says "I, Deborah, arose", so the song's "I" is feminine throughout.

decisions.choice: {{god_term:神|上帝}}
decisions.reason: The Chinese god_term setting, as in the earlier chapters: 神 by default, 上帝 as the reader's alternative, for every word naming the one God.

decisions.choice: Feminine ਗਾਵਾਂਗੀ, ਛੇੜਾਂਗੀ for the singer's 'I'
decisions.reason: Deborah leads the song (verse 7 'I, Deborah').

decisions.choice: "mga hari ... mga pinuno"
decisions.reason: The rulers of the nations, called to hear what Israel's God has done (m1).

decisions.choice: "Ako ... ako"
decisions.reason: The singer says "I" twice for emphasis (m2).

decisions.choice: "aawit ako ng papuri"
decisions.reason: Sing praise, often with instruments (m3).

source.text: יְהוָ֗ה בְּצֵאתְךָ֤ מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ בְּצַעְדְּךָ֙ מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֱד֔וֹם אֶ֣רֶץ רָעָ֔שָׁה גַּם־שָׁמַ֖יִם נָטָ֑פוּ גַּם־עָבִ֖ים נָ֥טְפוּ מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, in your going out from Seir, in your marching from [the] field of Edom, earth trembled, also heavens dripped, also clouds dripped water.

en.L: O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} went out from Seir, \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched from the field of Edom, \q [the] earth trembled, and [the] heavens dripped; \q yes, [the] clouds dripped water.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set out from Seir, \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} strode out from the land of Edom, \q the earth shook, the skies poured, \q the clouds poured down water.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} came out from Seir. \q You marched out from the land of Edom. \q Then the earth shook, and the sky poured rain. \q Water came pouring down from the clouds.

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ulipotoka Seiri, \q ulipopiga hatua kutoka shamba la Edomu, \q nchi ilitetemeka, [nazo] mbingu zikadondosha; \q naam, mawingu yakadondosha maji.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ulipoondoka Seiri, \q ulipotembea kwa nguvu kutoka nchi ya Edomu, \q nchi ilitikisika, mbingu zikamwaga, \q mawingu yakamwaga maji.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ulitoka Seiri. \q Ulitembea kutoka nchi ya Edomu. \q Ndipo nchi ikatikisika, na anga likamwaga mvua. \q Maji yakamiminika kutoka mawinguni.

es.L: Oh {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} saliste de Seír, \q cuando marchaste desde el campo de Edom, \q [la] tierra tembló, y [los] cielos gotearon; \q sí, [las] nubes gotearon agua.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} saliste de Seír, \q cuando avanzaste desde la tierra de Edom, \q la tierra se estremeció, los cielos se derramaron, \q las nubes derramaron agua.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} saliste de Seír. \q Marchaste desde la tierra de Edom. \q Entonces la tierra tembló, y del cielo cayó la lluvia. \q El agua caía a torrentes de las nubes.

fr.L: Ô {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sortis de Séir, \q quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} t’avanças depuis la campagne d’Édom, \q [la] terre trembla, et [les] cieux ruisselèrent ; \q oui, [les] nuées ruisselèrent d’eau.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} partis de Séir, \q quand {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} t’avanças depuis le pays d’Édom, \q la terre trembla, les cieux se déversèrent, \q les nuages déversèrent leurs eaux.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es sorti de Séir. \q Tu t’es avancé depuis le pays d’Édom. \q Alors la terre a tremblé, et le ciel a versé la pluie. \q L’eau est tombée à flots des nuages.

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra đi từ Sê-i-rơ, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tiến bước từ cánh đồng Ê-đôm, \q đất rung chuyển, các tầng trời cũng nhỏ giọt; \q phải, các đám mây nhỏ nước xuống.
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên đường từ Sê-i-rơ, \q khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sải bước ra từ đất Ê-đôm, \q thì đất rúng động, bầu trời đổ mưa, \q các đám mây trút nước xuống.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ra đi từ Sê-i-rơ. \q Ngài đã tiến bước ra từ đất Ê-đôm. \q Bấy giờ đất rung chuyển, và trời đổ mưa. \q Nước từ các đám mây tuôn đổ xuống.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주께서 세일에서 나오실 때에, \q 에돔 들에서 행진하실 때에, \q 땅이 흔들리고 하늘도 물을 떨어뜨렸습니다. \q 구름도 물을 쏟아부었습니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 세일에서 나오실 때에, \q 에돔 땅에서 힘차게 걸어 나오실 때에, \q 땅이 흔들리고 하늘이 쏟아붓고, \q 구름이 물을 쏟아 내렸습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님께서 세일에서 나오셨습니다. \q 에돔 땅에서 행진해 나오셨습니다. \q 그러자 땅이 흔들리고 하늘에서 비가 쏟아졌습니다. \q 구름에서 물이 쏟아져 내렸습니다.

pt.L: Ó {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} saíste de Seir, \q quando marchaste desde o campo de Edom, \q a terra tremeu, e os céus gotejaram; \q sim, as nuvens gotejaram água.
pt.B: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, quando {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} partiste de Seir, \q quando avançaste desde a terra de Edom, \q a terra estremeceu, os céus despejaram chuva, \q as nuvens derramaram água.
pt.R: {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} saíste de Seir. \q Marchaste desde a terra de Edom. \q Então a terra tremeu, e o céu despejou chuva. \q A água caiu das nuvens em torrentes.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ከሴይር በወጣህ ጊዜ፣ \q ከኤዶም ሜዳ በገሠገሥህ ጊዜ፣ \q ምድር ተንቀጠቀጠች፤ ሰማያትም አንጠባጠቡ፤ \q ደመናትም ውኃን አንጠባጠቡ።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ከሴይር በተነሣህ ጊዜ፣ \q ከኤዶም ምድር በተራመድህ ጊዜ፣ \q ምድር ተናወጠች፤ ሰማይም አፈሰሰ፤ \q ደመናትም ውኃ አወረዱ።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ፣ ከሴይር ወጣህ። \q ከኤዶም ምድር ተራመድህ። \q በዚያን ጊዜ ምድር ተናወጠች፤ ሰማዩም ዝናብ አፈሰሰ። \q ከደመናትም ውኃ ይወርድ ጀመር።

hi.L: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, जब तू सेईर से निकला, \q जब तू एदोम के मैदान से आगे बढ़ा, \q [तो] धरती काँप उठी, और आकाश टपकने लगा; \q हाँ, बादलों से पानी टपका।
hi.B: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, जब तू सेईर से निकल चला, \q जब तू एदोम के देश से क़दम बढ़ाता आया, \q तो धरती डोल उठी, आकाश बरस पड़ा, \q बादलों ने पानी उँडेल दिया।
hi.R: हे {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, तू सेईर से निकल आया। \q तू एदोम देश से आगे बढ़ा। \q तब धरती काँप उठी, और आकाश से वर्षा होने लगी। \q बादलों से पानी बरसने लगा।

ru.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, когда {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} выходил из Сеира, \q когда {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} шествовал с поля Едома, \q земля дрожала, и небеса капали, \q и облака проливали воду.
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, когда {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} выступил из Сеира, \q когда {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} шагал из земли Едома, \q земля сотрясалась, небеса изливались, \q облака проливали воду.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}, {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} вышел из Сеира. \q Ты пришёл из земли Едома. \q Тогда земля тряслась, и с неба лил дождь. \q Из облаков потоками лилась вода.

ja.L: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ、あなたがセイルから出て行かれたとき、 \q エドムの野から進み行かれたとき、 \q 地は震え、天もしたたり、 \q 雲も水をしたたらせた。
ja.B: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ、あなたがセイルから出て来られたとき、 \q エドムの地から進んで来られたとき、 \q 地は揺れ動き、天は降り注ぎ、 \q 雲は水を降り注いだ。
ja.R: {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}よ、あなたはセイルから出て来られた。 \q エドムの地から進んで来られた。 \q そのとき、地は揺れ、空から雨が降り注いだ。 \q 雲から水がどっと流れ落ちた。

uk.L: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, коли {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} виходив із Сеїру, \q коли {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} крокував з поля Едому, \q земля тремтіла, і небеса капали; \q так, хмари капали водою.
uk.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, коли {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} вирушив із Сеїру, \q коли {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} виступив із землі Едому, \q земля здригнулася, небо пролилося, \q хмари вилили воду.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Ягве}}, {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} вийшов із Сеїру. \q Ти виступив із землі Едому. \q Тоді земля затряслася, і з неба полив дощ. \q З хмар ринула вода.

id.L: Ya {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, ketika {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} keluar dari Seir, \q ketika {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} berjalan maju dari padang Edom, \q bumi gemetar, dan langit menitikkan air; \q ya, awan-awan menitikkan air.
id.B: Ya {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, ketika {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} keluar dari Seir, \q ketika {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} berjalan dari daerah Edom, \q bumi gemetar, langit mencurahkan hujan, \q dan awan-awan mencurahkan air.
id.R: {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:engkau|Engkau}} datang dari Seir. \q Engkau berjalan keluar dari tanah Edom. \q Lalu bumi berguncang, dan langit mencurahkan hujan. \q Air tercurah deras dari awan-awan.

zh.L: {{divine_name:上主|雅威}}啊，{{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从西珥出来的时候， \q {{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从以东的田野行进的时候， \q 地就震动，天也滴落， \q 云也滴下雨水。
zh.B: {{divine_name:上主|雅威}}啊，当{{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从西珥出发， \q 当{{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从以东地阔步前行， \q 大地震动，天空倾泻， \q 云层倾下雨水。
zh.R: {{divine_name:上主|雅威}}啊，{{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从西珥出来， \q {{deity_pronoun:你|祢}}从以东地出发前进。 \q 那时大地震动，天上下起大雨， \q 雨水从云中倾泻而下。

pa.L: ਹੇ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}}, ਜਦੋਂ ਤੂੰ ਸੇਈਰ ਤੋਂ ਨਿੱਕਲਿਆ, \q ਜਦੋਂ ਤੂੰ ਅਦੋਮ ਦੇ ਮੈਦਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਕੂਚ ਕੀਤਾ, \q ਧਰਤੀ ਕੰਬ ਗਈ, ਅਤੇ ਅਕਾਸ਼ ਚੋਣ ਲੱਗੇ; \q ਹਾਂ, ਬੱਦਲਾਂ ਨੇ ਪਾਣੀ ਚੋਇਆ।
pa.B: ਹੇ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}}, ਜਦੋਂ ਤੂੰ ਸੇਈਰ ਤੋਂ ਤੁਰਿਆ, \q ਜਦੋਂ ਤੂੰ ਅਦੋਮ ਦੀ ਧਰਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਪੁਲਾਂਘਾਂ ਭਰਦਾ ਨਿੱਕਲਿਆ, \q ਧਰਤੀ ਹਿੱਲ ਗਈ, ਅਕਾਸ਼ ਵਰ੍ਹ ਪਏ, \q ਬੱਦਲਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੋਹਲੇਧਾਰ ਪਾਣੀ ਵਰ੍ਹਾਇਆ।
pa.R: ਹੇ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}}, ਤੂੰ ਸੇਈਰ ਤੋਂ ਨਿੱਕਲ ਕੇ ਆਇਆ। \q ਤੂੰ ਅਦੋਮ ਦੀ ਧਰਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਕੂਚ ਕਰਦਾ ਆਇਆ। \q ਤਦ ਧਰਤੀ ਕੰਬੀ, ਅਤੇ ਅਸਮਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਮੀਂਹ ਵਰ੍ਹਿਆ। \q ਬੱਦਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪਾਣੀ ਹੀ ਪਾਣੀ ਡਿੱਗਿਆ।

tl.L: O {{divine_name:PANGINOON|Yahweh}}, nang lumabas {{deity_pronoun:ka|Ka}} mula sa Seir, \q nang lumakad {{deity_pronoun:ka|Ka}} mula sa parang ng Edom, \q ang lupa ay nayanig, at ang langit ay pumatak; \q oo, ang mga ulap ay nagpatak ng tubig.
tl.B: {{divine_name:PANGINOON|Yahweh}}, nang umalis {{deity_pronoun:ka|Ka}} mula sa Seir, \q nang humakbang {{deity_pronoun:ka|Ka}} mula sa lupain ng Edom, \q nayanig ang lupa, bumuhos ang langit, \q ang mga ulap ay nagbuhos ng tubig.
tl.R: {{divine_name:PANGINOON|Yahweh}}, lumabas {{deity_pronoun:ka|Ka}} mula sa Seir. \q Lumakad ka mula sa lupain ng Edom. \q Pagkatapos ay nayanig ang lupa, at bumuhos ang ulan mula sa langit. \q Bumuhos ang tubig mula sa mga ulap.

decisions.choice: Seir and Edom: the LORD comes from the mountains in the south, where he met Israel in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Seir is the mountain country of Edom, south of the Dead Sea. Other old poems picture the LORD coming from there as a warrior to help his people (Deuteronomy 33:2; Habakkuk 3:3; Psalm 68:8-9).

decisions.choice: the earth shook and the heavens poured rain: a great storm as the LORD comes
decisions.reason: The quaking earth and the pouring clouds picture the LORD's coming in storm. The rain explains how the Kishon swept the enemy away (verse 21) and why Sisera's chariots were no use (4:15).

decisions.choice: the land of Edom
decisions.reason: The word usually means a field; here it means the open country or territory of Edom.

decisions.choice: the sky poured rain
decisions.reason: The verb means "drip" or "pour"; Readable says what fell from the heavens.

decisions.choice: the vocative "SEIGNEUR" (without the article) under the divine name setting, and "tu" for the LORD with the deity pronoun setting, as in Psalms
decisions.reason: In the song Deborah turns to speak to the LORD. French addresses God with "tu", as the French style guide says, and the deity pronoun setting covers "tu", "te", "ton" where the English covers "you" and "your"; the sentence-initial "Tu" of Readable is written plainly, as "He" is in English. The divine name in address drops the article, as the Psalms do.

decisions.choice: the passé simple in the song where it tells what happened ("tu sortis", "la terre trembla") at Literal and Balanced, the passé composé at Readable
alternatives: the passé composé at every level, as in speech
decisions.reason: The song is a poem of praise sung by the narrator's heroes, and French poetry of this kind tells past events in the passé simple; Readable keeps its own rule and uses the passé composé, as it does in narrative.

decisions.choice: the singer speaks to the LORD as "Ngài" with "Lạy"
decisions.reason: As the psalmist does in the Vietnamese Psalms: "Lạy CHÚA" in address and "Ngài" with the deity_pronoun setting in the middle of a sentence.

decisions.choice: the singer speaks to God in the formal polite style (합쇼체), with "주께서" (L) and "주님께서" (B, R) for "you"
decisions.reason: As in Psalms, where a person speaking to God uses the formal polite style; Korean has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: tu (the singer to the LORD); você, vocês (the song to Deborah, Barak, the tribes, the hearers)
decisions.reason: For the whole song: the singer speaks to the LORD with "tu" ("saíste", "os teus inimigos", verse 31), as people speak to God throughout (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4), and the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting where the English has one. The song speaks to people with "vocês" and "você" (verses 2-3, 9-10, 12, 14, 16, 21, 23). The divine name stands alone in the call, "SENHOR", with no article.

decisions.choice: The song speaks to the LORD with "{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሆይ" and "አንተ" (verses 4 and 31).
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch, people speak to God with the familiar "you" of the Bible's prayers.

decisions.choice: "तू" to the LORD in the song
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch note and the style guide settle, people speaking to God say "तू", the intimate address of Hindi devotion. There are no deity_pronoun spans in Hindi (Devanagari has no capitals); respect for God comes from that address and from the honorific third person. This holds for the chapter.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:ГОСПОДИ|Яхве}}" for the name in the vocative, with "{{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}}"
decisions.reason: The song turns to speak to the LORD himself. The vocative of "ГОСПОДЬ" is "ГОСПОДИ", as the Pentateuch note sets; "Яхве" does not change. A "Ты" that begins a sentence is capitalised plainly.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:你|祢}} for the LORD addressed
decisions.reason: The singer speaks to the LORD with 你 in the deity_pronoun span (祢 by default), as the glossary has it for prayer and song; Readable's second line, where the English starts with an unspanned "You", takes the span too. 西珥 is Deuteronomy 1:44's form.

decisions.choice: ਤੂੰ to the LORD in the song
decisions.reason: Direct address to God, as in the Psalms and prayers elsewhere in Punjabi; third-person mentions keep the honorific plural.

decisions.choice: "Seir ... Edom"
decisions.reason: The LORD comes from the mountains in the south, where he met Israel in the wilderness (m1).

decisions.choice: "nayanig ang lupa ... pumatak ang langit"
decisions.reason: A great storm as the LORD comes (m2).

decisions.choice: "ka"
decisions.reason: God is addressed with the singular, as everywhere.

source.text: הָרִ֥ים נָזְל֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה זֶ֣ה סִינַ֔י מִפְּנֵ֕י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Mountains quaked before Yahweh, this [one of] Sinai, before Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.

en.L: [The] mountains quaked before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q this [One] of Sinai, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.B: The mountains quaked at the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the One of Sinai, at the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.
en.R: The mountains shook before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the God of Israel, the God who came to Mount Sinai.

sw.L: Milima ilitetemeka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q yule [wa] Sinai, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli.
sw.B: Milima ilitetemeka mbele ya uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q yule wa Sinai, mbele ya uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli.
sw.R: Milima ilitikisika mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q Mungu wa Israeli, Mungu aliyekuja kwenye Mlima Sinai.

es.L: [Los] montes se estremecieron ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q este [el] del Sinaí, ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.B: Los montes se estremecieron ante la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q el del Sinaí, ante la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel.
es.R: Los montes temblaron ante {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q el Dios de Israel, el Dios que vino al monte Sinaí.

fr.L: [Les] montagnes tremblèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q celui du Sinaï, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.B: Les montagnes chancelèrent en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q celui du Sinaï, en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.R: Les montagnes ont tremblé devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q le Dieu d’Israël, le Dieu qui est venu au mont Sinaï.

vi.L: Các núi rúng động trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q Đấng [của] Si-na-i này, trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Các núi rúng động trước sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q Đấng của Si-na-i, trước sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Các núi rung chuyển trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, Đấng đã ngự xuống núi Si-na-i.

ko.L: 산들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 진동하였다. \q 시내의 그분, 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서.
ko.B: 산들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 흔들렸다. \q 시내 산의 그분, 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 흔들렸다.
ko.R: 산들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 흔들렸다. \q 시내 산에 오셨던 하나님, 이스라엘의 하나님 앞에서 흔들렸다.

pt.L: Os montes tremeram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q Aquele do Sinai, diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.B: Os montes tremeram na presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q Aquele do Sinai, na presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, o Deus de Israel.
pt.R: Os montes tremeram diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, \q o Deus de Israel, o Deus que veio ao monte Sinai.

am.L: ተራሮች {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ተናወጡ፤ \q ይህ የሲናው [አምላክ]፣ በእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት።
am.B: ተራሮች {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ተንቀጠቀጡ፤ \q የሲናው አምላክ፣ በእስራኤል አምላክ {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት።
am.R: ተራሮች {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ፊት ተናወጡ፤ \q እርሱ የእስራኤል አምላክ፣ ወደ ሲና ተራራ የመጣው አምላክ ነው።

hi.L: पहाड़ {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के सामने काँप उठे, \q यह सीनै वाला, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर के सामने।
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की उपस्थिति से पहाड़ काँप उठे, \q सीनै वाले की उपस्थिति से, {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}}, इस्राएल के परमेश्वर की उपस्थिति से।
hi.R: पहाड़ {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के सामने काँप उठे, \q इस्राएल के परमेश्वर के सामने, जो सीनै पहाड़ पर उतरे थे।

ru.L: Горы сотрясались перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, \q этот [Бог] Синая, перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, Богом Израиля.
ru.B: Горы содрогались перед лицом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, \q Того, кто явился на Синае, перед лицом {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, Бога Израиля.
ru.R: Горы тряслись перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, \q перед Богом Израиля, Богом, который пришёл на гору Синай.

ja.L: 山々は{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の前で揺れ動いた。 \q シナイのあの方、イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の前で。
ja.B: 山々は{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の前で揺れ動いた。 \q シナイの方、イスラエルの神、{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の前で。
ja.R: 山々は{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}の前で震えた。 \q イスラエルの神、シナイ山に来られた神の前で。

uk.L: Гори здригнулися перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДОМ|Ягве}}, \q цей [Той] із Синаю, перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДОМ|Ягве}}, Богом Ізраїля.
uk.B: Гори затремтіли перед обличчям {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, \q Того, що із Синаю, перед обличчям {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}, Бога Ізраїля.
uk.R: Гори затряслися перед {{divine_name:ГОСПОДОМ|Ягве}}, \q Богом Ізраїля, Богом, що прийшов на гору Синай.

id.L: Gunung-gunung bergoyang di hadapan {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, \q Dia yang [dari] Sinai, di hadapan {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, Allah Israel.
id.B: Gunung-gunung bergoncang di hadapan {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, \q Dia yang dari Sinai, di hadapan {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, Allah Israel.
id.R: Gunung-gunung berguncang di hadapan {{divine_name:TUHAN|Yahweh}}, \q Allah Israel, Allah yang datang ke gunung Sinai.

zh.L: 众山在{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}面前摇撼， \q 这西奈的[那位]，在{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}面前。
zh.B: 众山在{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}面前震动， \q 在西奈的那一位面前，在{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}面前。
zh.R: 众山在{{divine_name:上主|雅威}}面前震动， \q 在以色列的{{god_term:神|上帝}}、曾降临西奈山的{{god_term:神|上帝}}面前。

pa.L: ਪਹਾੜ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਦੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਥਰਥਰਾ ਗਏ, \q ਸੀਨਈ ਵਾਲੇ ਇਸ [ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ] ਦੇ ਅੱਗੇ, {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}}, ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ ਦੇ ਅੱਗੇ।
pa.B: {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਦੀ ਹਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਹਾੜ ਥਰਥਰਾਏ, \q ਸੀਨਈ ਵਾਲੇ ਦੀ ਹਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਵਿੱਚ, ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਦੀ ਹਜ਼ੂਰੀ ਵਿੱਚ।
pa.R: {{divine_name:ਪ੍ਰਭੂ|ਯਾਹਵੇ}} ਅੱਗੇ ਪਹਾੜ ਕੰਬ ਉੱਠੇ, \q ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ ਅੱਗੇ, ਉਸ ਪਰਮੇਸ਼ੁਰ ਅੱਗੇ ਜਿਹੜੇ ਸੀਨਈ ਪਰਬਤ ਉੱਤੇ ਆਏ ਸਨ।

tl.L: Ang mga bundok ay nayanig sa harap {{divine_name:ng PANGINOON|ni Yahweh}}, \q ito [na nasa] Sinai, sa harap {{divine_name:ng PANGINOON|ni Yahweh}}, ang Diyos ng Israel.
tl.B: Nayanig ang mga bundok sa harapan {{divine_name:ng PANGINOON|ni Yahweh}}, \q ang Isang nasa Sinai, sa harapan {{divine_name:ng PANGINOON|ni Yahweh}}, ang Diyos ng Israel.
tl.R: Nayanig ang mga bundok sa harap {{divine_name:ng PANGINOON|ni Yahweh}}, \q ang Diyos ng Israel, ang Diyos na dumating sa Bundok Sinai.

decisions.choice: quaked: shook before the LORD
decisions.reason: As the vowels are written, the verb would mean "flowed", picturing the mountains streaming or melting. Read as the verb "quake", it says the mountains shook, as in Isaiah 63:19 and 64:2, and the ancient Greek translation reads "shook". Both picture the mountains overcome by the LORD's coming.

decisions.choice: the One of Sinai: a title of the LORD, the God who appeared at Sinai
decisions.reason: The short word "this" can work as "the one of" in old Hebrew poetry, and Psalm 68:9 uses the same phrase as a title of God. The other reading is "even Sinai": Sinai itself quaked before the LORD (Exodus 19:18).

decisions.choice: the God who came to Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title: the LORD is known as the God who came down on Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:18-20).

decisions.choice: "Đấng [của] Si-na-i" (L); "Đấng của Si-na-i" (B)
decisions.reason: A title of the LORD (m2), worded as in the Vietnamese Psalm 68:8, which uses the same title.

decisions.choice: Aquele do Sinai
decisions.reason: The phrase is taken as a title of the LORD (m2), and "Aquele do Sinai", capitalised, says that in Portuguese without supplying a noun, as the English supplies "One".

decisions.choice: "этот [Бог] Синая" (L); "Тот, кто явился на Синае" (B); "Бог, который пришёл на гору Синай" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is read as a title of the LORD, the One of Sinai (m2), not as the mountain itself shaking. Literal supplies "Бог" in brackets; the capital "Тот" at Balanced is the title, not a pronoun, and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: "this [One] of Sinai": "シナイのあの方" (L), "シナイの方" (B), "シナイ山に来られた神" (R)
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m2 (uncertain): a title of the LORD, the God who appeared at Sinai.

decisions.choice: "Dia yang dari Sinai", with "Dia" in a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The title of the LORD (m2) as a pronoun phrase, "the One of Sinai"; Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nayanig"
decisions.reason: Shook before the LORD (m1).

decisions.choice: "ito na nasa Sinai"
decisions.reason: A title of the LORD, the God who appeared at Sinai (m2).

source.text: בִּימֵ֞י שַׁמְגַּ֤ר בֶּן־עֲנָת֙ בִּימֵ֣י יָעֵ֔ל חָדְל֖וּ אֳרָח֑וֹת וְהֹלְכֵ֣י נְתִיב֔וֹת יֵלְכ֕וּ אֳרָח֖וֹת עֲקַלְקַלּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] days of Shamgar son of Anath, in [the] days of Jael, ceased roads, and walkers of paths walked roads winding.

en.L: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, \q [the] roads ceased, \q and those walking the paths walked [by] winding roads.
en.B: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, in the time of Jael, \q the highways lay empty, \q and travelers went by crooked side roads.
en.R: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath and in the days of Jael, \q no one traveled on the main roads. \q Anyone who had to go somewhere took winding back roads.

sw.L: Katika siku za Shamgari mwana wa Anathi, katika siku za Yaeli, \q njia kuu zilikoma, \q nao wapita njia wakapita [kwa] njia za kuzunguka.
sw.B: Wakati wa Shamgari mwana wa Anathi, wakati wa Yaeli, \q barabara kuu zilikuwa tupu, \q nao wasafiri walipita njia za pembeni zilizopinda.
sw.R: Katika siku za Shamgari mwana wa Anathi na katika siku za Yaeli, \q hakuna aliyesafiri kwenye barabara kuu. \q Yeyote aliyelazimika kwenda mahali fulani alipita vichochoro vilivyopindapinda.

es.L: En los días de Samgar hijo de Anat, en los días de Jael, \q cesaron [los] caminos, \q y los que andaban por las sendas andaban [por] caminos tortuosos.
es.B: En tiempos de Samgar hijo de Anat, en tiempos de Jael, \q los caminos quedaron desiertos, \q y los viajeros iban por senderos torcidos.
es.R: En los días de Samgar hijo de Anat y en los días de Jael, \q nadie viajaba por los caminos principales. \q Quien tenía que ir a algún lugar tomaba senderos escondidos y con muchas vueltas.

fr.L: Aux jours de Shamgar, fils d’Anath, aux jours de Yaël, \q [les] routes cessèrent, \q et ceux qui allaient par les sentiers allèrent [par] des routes tortueuses.
fr.B: Au temps de Shamgar, fils d’Anath, au temps de Yaël, \q les grandes routes étaient désertes, \q et les voyageurs prenaient des chemins détournés.
fr.R: Au temps de Shamgar, fils d’Anath, et au temps de Yaël, \q personne ne passait par les grandes routes. \q Ceux qui devaient voyager prenaient de petits chemins détournés.

vi.L: Trong những ngày của Sam-ga con trai A-nát, trong những ngày của Gia-ên, \q các con đường lớn bỏ không, \q và những người đi đường phải đi [theo] những lối quanh co.
vi.B: Vào thời Sam-ga con trai A-nát, vào thời Gia-ên, \q các đường cái vắng tanh, \q và khách đi đường phải theo những lối nhỏ quanh co.
vi.R: Trong thời Sam-ga con trai A-nát và trong thời Gia-ên, \q không ai đi trên các đường lớn. \q Ai cần đi đâu cũng phải theo những lối mòn quanh co.

ko.L: 아낫의 아들 삼갈의 날에, 야엘의 날에, \q 큰길들이 끊어졌고, \q 길을 다니는 사람들은 구불구불한 길[로] 다녔다.
ko.B: 아낫의 아들 삼갈 때에, 야엘 때에, \q 큰길에는 사람이 끊어지고, \q 나그네들은 구불구불한 뒷길로 다녔다.
ko.R: 아낫의 아들 삼갈 때와 야엘 때에는 \q 아무도 큰길로 다니지 않았다. \q 어디를 가야 하는 사람은 구불구불한 뒷길로 다녔다.

pt.L: Nos dias de Sangar, filho de Anate, nos dias de Jael, \q as estradas cessaram, \q e os que andavam pelas veredas andavam [por] caminhos tortuosos.
pt.B: No tempo de Sangar, filho de Anate, no tempo de Jael, \q as estradas ficaram vazias, \q e os viajantes iam por atalhos tortuosos.
pt.R: Nos dias de Sangar, filho de Anate, e nos dias de Jael, \q ninguém viajava pelas estradas principais. \q Quem precisava ir a algum lugar ia por caminhos escondidos e cheios de curvas.

am.L: በዓናት ልጅ በሰሜጋር ዘመን፣ በኢያኤል ዘመን፣ \q መንገዶች ቀሩ፤ \q በጎዳና የሚሄዱም በጠማማ መንገድ ሄዱ።
am.B: በዓናት ልጅ በሰሜጋር ዘመን፣ በኢያኤል ዘመን፣ \q አውራ ጎዳናዎቹ ባዶ ሆኑ፤ \q መንገደኞችም በጠመዝማዛ የጎን መንገዶች ሄዱ።
am.R: በዓናት ልጅ በሰሜጋርና በኢያኤል ዘመን \q ማንም በዋና መንገዶች አይሄድም ነበር። \q መሄድ ያለበት ሰው ሁሉ ጠመዝማዛ በሆኑ የጓሮ መንገዶች ይሄድ ነበር።

hi.L: अनात के पुत्र शमगर के दिनों में, याएल के दिनों में, \q राजमार्ग सूने पड़ गए, \q और पगडंडियों पर चलनेवाले टेढ़े-मेढ़े रास्तों से चलते थे।
hi.B: अनात के पुत्र शमगर के समय में, याएल के समय में, \q राजमार्ग सूने पड़े थे, \q और यात्री टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी पगडंडियों से जाते थे।
hi.R: अनात के पुत्र शमगर के दिनों में और याएल के दिनों में \q बड़ी सड़कों पर कोई नहीं चलता था। \q जिसे कहीं जाना होता, वह घुमावदार छोटे रास्तों से जाता था।

ru.L: Во дни Самегара, сына Анафа, во дни Иаили \q прекратились дороги, \q и ходившие путями ходили окольными дорогами.
ru.B: Во времена Самегара, сына Анафа, во времена Иаили \q большие дороги опустели, \q а путники ходили кривыми тропами.
ru.R: Во дни Самегара, сына Анафа, и во дни Иаили \q никто не ходил по большим дорогам. \q Кому нужно было куда-то идти, шли извилистыми тропинками.

ja.L: アナトの子シャムガルの日々に、ヤエルの日々に、 \q 大路は絶え、 \q 道を行く者たちは曲がりくねった道を行った。
ja.B: アナトの子シャムガルの時代、ヤエルの時代には、 \q 大路は人通りが絶え、 \q 旅人は曲がりくねった脇道を行った。
ja.R: アナトの息子シャムガルの時代にも、ヤエルの時代にも、 \q 大きな道を通る人はだれもいなかった。 \q どこかへ行かなければならない人は、曲がりくねった裏道を通った。

uk.L: За днів Шамгара, сина Анати, за днів Яїлі, \q припинилися дороги, \q і ті, що ходили стежками, ходили звивистими дорогами.
uk.B: За часів Шамгара, сина Анати, за часів Яїлі, \q биті шляхи спорожніли, \q і подорожні ходили манівцями.
uk.R: За днів Шамгара, сина Анати, і за днів Яїлі \q ніхто не ходив головними шляхами. \q Кому треба було кудись іти, той ходив покрученими бічними стежками.

id.L: Pada zaman Samgar anak Anat, pada zaman Yael, \q jalan-jalan raya sepi, \q dan orang yang berjalan di jalan-jalan menempuh jalan yang berliku-liku.
id.B: Pada zaman Samgar anak Anat, pada zaman Yael, \q jalan-jalan raya sunyi, \q dan para pengembara menempuh jalan-jalan yang berliku-liku.
id.R: Pada zaman Samgar anak Anat dan pada zaman Yael, \q tidak ada orang yang lewat di jalan-jalan besar. \q Siapa saja yang harus bepergian menempuh jalan-jalan kecil yang berliku-liku.

zh.L: 在亚纳的儿子珊迦的日子，在雅亿的日子， \q 大路断绝， \q 走路的人都走弯曲的小路。
zh.B: 在亚纳的儿子珊迦的时代，在雅亿的时代， \q 大道空无一人， \q 旅人只好走偏僻弯曲的小道。
zh.R: 在亚纳的儿子珊迦的日子，在雅亿的日子， \q 没有人敢在大路上走。 \q 要出门的人都走弯弯曲曲的小路。

pa.L: ਅਨਾਥ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਮਗਰ ਦੇ ਦਿਨੀਂ, ਯਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਦਿਨੀਂ, \q ਸੜਕਾਂ ਸੁੰਨੀਆਂ ਹੋ ਗਈਆਂ, \q ਅਤੇ ਰਾਹੀ ਵਿੰਗੇ-ਟੇਢੇ ਰਾਹਾਂ ਥਾਣੀਂ ਤੁਰਦੇ ਸਨ।
pa.B: ਅਨਾਥ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਮਗਰ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ, ਯਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ, \q ਵੱਡੇ ਰਾਹ ਵਿਰਾਨ ਪਏ ਸਨ, \q ਅਤੇ ਮੁਸਾਫ਼ਰ ਲੁਕਵੀਆਂ ਪਗਡੰਡੀਆਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਤੁਰਦੇ ਸਨ।
pa.R: ਅਨਾਥ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤਰ ਸ਼ਮਗਰ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਅਤੇ ਯਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਸਮੇਂ \q ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਸੜਕਾਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਤੁਰਦਾ ਸੀ। \q ਜਿਸ ਕਿਸੇ ਨੇ ਕਿਤੇ ਜਾਣਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ, ਉਹ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਵਿੰਗੇ ਰਾਹਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਸੀ।

tl.L: Sa mga araw ni Shamgar na anak ni Anat, sa mga araw ni Jael, \q ang mga daan ay naglaho, \q at ang mga naglalakbay sa mga landas ay lumakad [sa] mga paliku-likong daan.
tl.B: Noong panahon ni Shamgar na anak ni Anat, noong panahon ni Jael, \q walang laman ang mga lansangan, \q at ang mga manlalakbay ay dumaan sa mga liku-likong daan sa gilid.
tl.R: Noong mga araw ni Shamgar na anak ni Anat at noong mga araw ni Jael, \q walang naglalakbay sa malalaking daan. \q Ang sinumang kailangang pumunta sa kung saan ay dumaraan sa mga liku-likong daan sa likuran.

decisions.choice: Shamgar and Jael: the time just before the victory, when Canaan oppressed Israel
decisions.reason: Shamgar son of Anath fought the Philistines (3:31); Jael is the woman who killed Sisera (4:17-22; verses 24-27). The song dates the hard years by them.

decisions.choice: the roads ceased: the main roads were deserted
decisions.reason: With other vowels the same letters mean "caravans": "the caravans stopped". Either way, trade and travel had stopped because the roads were unsafe.

decisions.choice: those who had to travel used winding paths, to stay out of sight of raiders
decisions.reason: The contrast is between the open main roads and twisting byways where travelers could hide.

decisions.choice: lay empty (Balanced); no one traveled on (Readable)
decisions.reason: Roads "ceasing" means no one used them; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "Shamgar ... Jael"
decisions.reason: The time just before the victory, when Canaan oppressed Israel (m1).

decisions.choice: "ang mga daan ay naglaho"
decisions.reason: The main roads were deserted (m2).

decisions.choice: "mga paliku-likong daan"
decisions.reason: Those who had to travel used winding paths, to stay out of sight of raiders (m3).

source.text: חָדְל֧וּ פְרָז֛וֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חָדֵ֑לּוּ עַ֤ד שַׁקַּ֨מְתִּי֙ דְּבוֹרָ֔ה שַׁקַּ֥מְתִּי אֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Ceased villagers in Israel, they ceased, until that I arose, Deborah, that I arose, a mother in Israel.

en.L: [The] villagers ceased in Israel; they ceased, \q until I, Deborah, arose, \q [until] I arose, a mother in Israel.
en.B: The villages of Israel were deserted, deserted, \q until I, Deborah, arose, \q until I arose, a mother in Israel.
en.R: No one was left in the villages of Israel, no one, \q until I, Deborah, rose up, \q until I rose up like a mother for Israel.

sw.L: Wanavijiji walikoma katika Israeli; walikoma, \q hata nilipoinuka mimi, Debora, \q [hata] nilipoinuka, mama katika Israeli.
sw.B: Vijiji vya Israeli viliachwa tupu, tupu kabisa, \q hata nilipoinuka mimi, Debora, \q hata nilipoinuka, mama katika Israeli.
sw.R: Hakuna aliyebaki katika vijiji vya Israeli, hakuna, \q hata nilipoinuka mimi, Debora, \q hata nilipoinuka kama mama kwa ajili ya Israeli.

es.L: Cesaron [los] aldeanos en Israel; cesaron, \q hasta que yo, Débora, me levanté, \q [hasta que] me levanté, una madre en Israel.
es.B: Las aldeas de Israel quedaron desiertas, desiertas, \q hasta que yo, Débora, me levanté, \q hasta que me levanté, una madre en Israel.
es.R: No quedaba nadie en las aldeas de Israel, nadie, \q hasta que yo, Débora, me levanté, \q hasta que me levanté como una madre para Israel.

fr.L: [Les] villageois cessèrent en Israël, ils cessèrent, \q jusqu’à ce que je me sois levée, moi, Débora, \q [jusqu’à ce] que je me sois levée, une mère en Israël.
fr.B: Les villages d’Israël étaient désertés, désertés, \q jusqu’à ce que je me lève, moi, Débora, \q jusqu’à ce que je me lève, mère en Israël.
fr.R: Il ne restait plus personne dans les villages d’Israël, plus personne, \q jusqu’au jour où moi, Débora, je me suis levée, \q où je me suis levée comme une mère pour Israël.

vi.L: Dân làng ngưng bặt trong Y-sơ-ra-ên; họ ngưng bặt, \q cho đến khi tôi, Đê-bô-ra, đứng lên, \q [cho đến khi] tôi đứng lên, một người mẹ trong Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.B: Các làng mạc Y-sơ-ra-ên bỏ hoang, bỏ hoang, \q cho đến khi tôi, Đê-bô-ra, đứng lên, \q cho đến khi tôi đứng lên, một người mẹ trong Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Trong các làng của Y-sơ-ra-ên không còn ai, không còn ai cả, \q cho đến khi tôi, Đê-bô-ra, đứng lên, \q cho đến khi tôi đứng lên như một người mẹ của Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 이스라엘에 마을 사람들이 끊어졌다. 끊어졌다. \q 나 드보라가 일어날 때까지, \q 이스라엘의 어머니인 내가 일어날 때까지.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 마을들이 비었다. 텅 비었다. \q 나 드보라가 일어날 때까지, \q 이스라엘의 어머니인 내가 일어날 때까지.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 마을에는 아무도 남지 않았다. 아무도. \q 나 드보라가 일어날 때까지, \q 이스라엘을 위해 어머니처럼 내가 일어날 때까지.

pt.L: Cessaram os aldeões em Israel; cessaram, \q até que eu, Débora, me levantei, \q [até que] me levantei, mãe em Israel.
pt.B: As aldeias de Israel ficaram desertas, desertas, \q até que eu, Débora, me levantei, \q até que me levantei, mãe em Israel.
pt.R: Não restou ninguém nas aldeias de Israel, ninguém, \q até que eu, Débora, me levantei, \q até que me levantei como mãe de Israel.

am.L: በእስራኤል የመንደር ሰዎች ቀሩ፤ ቀሩ፤ \q እኔ ዲቦራ እስክነሣ ድረስ፣ \q በእስራኤል እናት ሆኜ እስክነሣ ድረስ።
am.B: የእስራኤል መንደሮች ባዶ ሆኑ፤ ባዶ ሆኑ፤ \q እኔ ዲቦራ እስክነሣ ድረስ፣ \q በእስራኤል እናት ሆኜ እስክነሣ ድረስ።
am.R: በእስራኤል መንደሮች ማንም አልቀረም፤ ማንም፤ \q እኔ ዲቦራ እስክነሣ ድረስ፣ \q ለእስራኤል እንደ እናት ሆኜ እስክነሣ ድረስ።

hi.L: इस्राएल में गाँववाले मिट गए, वे मिट गए, \q जब तक मैं, दबोरा, न उठी, \q [जब तक] मैं न उठी, इस्राएल में एक माता।
hi.B: इस्राएल के गाँव उजड़ गए, उजड़ गए, \q जब तक मैं, दबोरा, न उठी, \q जब तक मैं न उठी, इस्राएल में एक माता बनकर।
hi.R: इस्राएल के गाँवों में कोई नहीं बचा, कोई भी नहीं, \q जब तक मैं, दबोरा, न उठी, \q जब तक मैं इस्राएल के लिए माँ बनकर न उठी।

ru.L: Прекратились поселяне в Израиле, прекратились, \q пока не встала я, Девора, \q [пока] не встала я, мать в Израиле.
ru.B: Опустели селения Израиля, опустели, \q пока не поднялась я, Девора, \q пока не поднялась я, мать в Израиле.
ru.R: В селениях Израиля никого не осталось, никого, \q пока не поднялась я, Девора, \q пока я не поднялась, как мать, за Израиль.

ja.L: イスラエルで村人たちは絶えた。彼らは絶えた。 \q わたし、デボラが立ち上がるまで、 \q イスラエルの母として、わたしが立ち上がるまで。
ja.B: イスラエルの村々は荒れ果てた。荒れ果てた。 \q わたし、デボラが立ち上がるまで、 \q イスラエルの母として、わたしが立ち上がるまで。
ja.R: イスラエルの村々には、だれもいなくなった。だれも。 \q わたし、デボラが立ち上がるまで。 \q わたしが、イスラエルのために母のように立ち上がるまで。

uk.L: Не стало сільських мешканців в Ізраїлі; не стало, \q аж поки я, Девора, не встала, \q [аж поки] я не встала, мати в Ізраїлі.
uk.B: Опустіли села Ізраїля, опустіли, \q аж поки я, Девора, не встала, \q аж поки я не встала, мати в Ізраїлі.
uk.R: Нікого не лишилося в селах Ізраїля, нікого, \q аж поки я, Девора, не піднялася, \q аж поки я не піднялася, наче мати для Ізраїля.

id.L: Penduduk desa lenyap di Israel; mereka lenyap, \q sampai aku, Debora, bangkit, \q [sampai] aku bangkit, seorang ibu di Israel.
id.B: Kehidupan desa terhenti di Israel, terhenti, \q sampai aku, Debora, bangkit, \q sampai aku bangkit sebagai ibu di Israel.
id.R: Tidak ada lagi orang di desa-desa Israel, tidak ada, \q sampai aku, Debora, bangkit, \q sampai aku bangkit seperti seorang ibu bagi Israel.

zh.L: 以色列中的村民断绝了，断绝了， \q 直到我，就是底波拉，起来， \q [直到]我起来，作以色列中的母亲。
zh.B: 以色列的村庄荒凉了，荒凉无人， \q 等到我底波拉站了起来， \q 等到我站起来，成为以色列的母亲。
zh.R: 以色列的村庄里没有人留下，一个也没有， \q 直到我，底波拉，挺身而出， \q 直到我挺身而出，像母亲一样照顾以色列。

pa.L: ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ ਦੇ ਵਾਸੀ ਮੁੱਕ ਗਏ; ਉਹ ਮੁੱਕ ਗਏ, \q ਜਦ ਤੱਕ ਮੈਂ, ਦਬੋਰਾਹ, ਉੱਠ ਨਾ ਖਲੋਤੀ, \q [ਜਦ ਤੱਕ] ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਮੈਂ ਉੱਠ ਨਾ ਖਲੋਤੀ।
pa.B: ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡ ਉੱਜੜ ਗਏ, ਉੱਜੜ ਗਏ, \q ਜਦ ਤੱਕ ਮੈਂ, ਦਬੋਰਾਹ, ਉੱਠ ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਨਾ ਹੋਈ, \q ਜਦ ਤੱਕ ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੈਂ ਮਾਂ ਬਣ ਕੇ ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਨਾ ਹੋਈ।
pa.R: ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਪਿੰਡਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੋਈ ਨਾ ਰਿਹਾ, ਕੋਈ ਵੀ ਨਾ, \q ਜਦ ਤੱਕ ਮੈਂ, ਦਬੋਰਾਹ, ਉੱਠੀ ਨਹੀਂ, \q ਜਦ ਤੱਕ ਮੈਂ ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਲਈ ਮਾਂ ਵਾਂਗ ਉੱਠੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

tl.L: Naglaho ang mga taganayon sa Israel; naglaho sila, \q hanggang sa tumindig ako, si Debora, \q [hanggang] tumindig ako, isang ina sa Israel.
tl.B: Naiwang walang tao ang mga nayon ng Israel, walang tao, \q hanggang sa tumindig ako, si Debora, \q hanggang sa tumindig ako, isang ina sa Israel.
tl.R: Walang naiwan sa mga nayon ng Israel, wala ni isa, \q hanggang sa bumangon ako, si Debora, \q hanggang sa bumangon ako na parang isang ina para sa Israel.

decisions.choice: villagers: the people of open country villages; village life came to an end
decisions.reason: The word is related to the one for unwalled villages (Deuteronomy 3:5; Esther 9:19), so the line says the countryside was emptied, as the roads were (verse 6). Others take it as "warriors" or "leaders": "the warriors held back in Israel". The word comes again in verse 11.

decisions.choice: I arose: Deborah speaks of herself
decisions.reason: As the text is written, the verb is "I arose". The same ending was also an old form of "you" said to a woman, which gives "until you arose, Deborah"; verse 12 speaks to Deborah in the same way. The meaning is the same: the change came when Deborah stood up to lead.

decisions.choice: a mother in Israel: a leader who protects and cares for the people
decisions.reason: The title is used of a city that sustains its people in 2 Samuel 20:19. It honors Deborah as one who looked after Israel, not as the mother of children.

decisions.choice: the villages were deserted (Balanced); no one was left in the villages (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb "ceased" means the village people were gone; Balanced and Readable say it of the villages.

decisions.choice: "một người mẹ trong Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L, B); "như một người mẹ của Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: A leader who protects and cares for the people (m3); Readable makes the picture a comparison, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: os aldeões (L); as aldeias ... desertas (B); ninguém nas aldeias (R)
decisions.reason: Following m1, the word is the people of the open villages: Literal says "aldeões" (also verse 11), and Balanced and Readable say it of the villages, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "a mother in Israel": "イスラエルの母として" (L, B), "イスラエルのために母のように" (R)
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m3: a leader who protects and cares for the people.

decisions.choice: "起来" (L), "站了起来" (B), "挺身而出" (R) for "I arose"
decisions.reason: Deborah's rising to lead, drafted afresh; 兴起 is kept for the LORD raising up judges (2:16).

decisions.choice: "mga taganayon"
decisions.reason: The people of open country villages; village life came to an end (m1).

decisions.choice: "tumindig ako"
decisions.reason: Deborah speaks of herself (m2).

decisions.choice: "isang ina sa Israel"
decisions.reason: A leader who protects and cares for the people (m3).

source.text: יִבְחַר֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אָ֖ז לָחֶ֣ם שְׁעָרִ֑ים מָגֵ֤ן אִם־יֵֽרָאֶה֙ וָרֹ֔מַח בְּאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: He chose gods new; then war [was in the] gates; shield, if it was seen, and spear, among forty thousand in Israel?

en.L: [Israel] chose new gods; \q then war [was at the] gates. \q Was a shield seen, or a spear, \q among forty thousand in Israel?
en.B: Israel chose new gods; \q then war came to the city gates. \q Not a shield or spear was to be seen \q among forty thousand in Israel.
en.R: Israel chose to worship new gods, \q and then war came right up to the city gates. \q Not one shield or spear could be found \q among forty thousand in Israel.

sw.L: [Israeli] walichagua miungu mipya; \q ndipo vita [vikawa] malangoni. \q Je, ngao ilionekana, au mkuki, \q kati ya elfu arobaini katika Israeli?
sw.B: Israeli walichagua miungu mipya; \q ndipo vita vikafika kwenye malango ya miji. \q Haikuonekana ngao wala mkuki \q kati ya watu elfu arobaini katika Israeli.
sw.R: Israeli walichagua kuabudu miungu mipya, \q kisha vita vikafika mpaka malangoni mwa miji. \q Haikupatikana hata ngao moja wala mkuki \q kati ya watu elfu arobaini katika Israeli.

es.L: [Israel] escogió dioses nuevos; \q entonces [hubo] guerra [a las] puertas. \q ¿Se veía un escudo, o una lanza, \q entre cuarenta mil en Israel?
es.B: Israel escogió dioses nuevos; \q entonces la guerra llegó a las puertas de las ciudades. \q No se veía ni escudo ni lanza \q entre cuarenta mil en Israel.
es.R: Israel decidió adorar a dioses nuevos, \q y entonces la guerra llegó hasta las puertas de las ciudades. \q No se podía encontrar ni un escudo ni una lanza \q entre cuarenta mil en Israel.

fr.L: [Israël] choisit des dieux nouveaux ; \q alors la guerre [fut aux] portes. \q Voyait-on un bouclier ou une lance \q parmi quarante mille en Israël ?
fr.B: Israël se choisit des dieux nouveaux ; \q alors la guerre vint aux portes des villes. \q On ne voyait ni bouclier ni lance \q parmi quarante mille hommes en Israël.
fr.R: Israël a choisi d’adorer des dieux nouveaux, \q et alors la guerre est arrivée jusqu’aux portes des villes. \q On ne pouvait pas trouver un seul bouclier ni une seule lance \q parmi quarante mille hommes en Israël.

vi.L: [Y-sơ-ra-ên] đã chọn các thần mới; \q bấy giờ chiến tranh [đến tận] cổng thành. \q Có thấy một cái khiên, hay một ngọn giáo, \q giữa bốn mươi nghìn người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên không?
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã chọn các thần mới; \q bấy giờ chiến tranh kéo đến tận cổng thành. \q Chẳng thấy một cái khiên hay một ngọn giáo nào \q giữa bốn mươi nghìn người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên.
vi.R: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã chọn thờ các thần mới, \q và rồi chiến tranh kéo đến ngay cổng thành. \q Không tìm được một cái khiên hay ngọn giáo nào \q giữa bốn mươi nghìn người trong Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: [이스라엘이] 새 신들을 택하였다. \q 그러자 전쟁이 성문[에 이르렀다]. \q 이스라엘의 사만 명 가운데 \q 방패나 창이 보였더냐?
ko.B: 이스라엘이 새 신들을 택하니, \q 전쟁이 성문에까지 밀어닥쳤다. \q 이스라엘의 사만 명 가운데 \q 방패도 창도 보이지 않았다.
ko.R: 이스라엘이 새 신들을 섬기기로 하자, \q 전쟁이 바로 성문 앞까지 닥쳐왔다. \q 이스라엘의 사만 명 가운데 \q 방패나 창을 가진 사람이 하나도 없었다.

pt.L: [Israel] escolheu deuses novos; \q então [houve] guerra [às] portas. \q Via-se escudo ou lança \q entre quarenta mil em Israel?
pt.B: Israel escolheu deuses novos; \q então a guerra chegou às portas das cidades. \q Não se via escudo nem lança \q entre quarenta mil em Israel.
pt.R: Israel escolheu adorar deuses novos, \q e então a guerra chegou até as portas das cidades. \q Não se achava nem um escudo nem uma lança \q entre quarenta mil em Israel.

am.L: [እስራኤል] አዳዲስ አማልክትን መረጠ፤ \q ያን ጊዜ ጦርነት በደጆች [ነበረ]። \q ጋሻ ወይም ጦር ታየን፣ \q በእስራኤል ካሉት ከአርባ ሺህ መካከል?
am.B: እስራኤል አዳዲስ አማልክትን መረጠ፤ \q ያን ጊዜ ጦርነት እስከ ከተማ በሮች መጣ። \q ጋሻም ሆነ ጦር አልታየም \q በእስራኤል ከነበሩት ከአርባ ሺህ መካከል።
am.R: እስራኤል አዳዲስ አማልክትን ማምለክ መረጠ፤ \q ከዚያም ጦርነት እስከ ከተማ በሮች ድረስ መጣ። \q አንድም ጋሻ ወይም ጦር አልተገኘም \q በእስራኤል ከነበሩት ከአርባ ሺህ መካከል።

hi.L: [इस्राएल ने] नए देवता चुने; \q तब फाटकों पर युद्ध [था]। \q क्या ढाल या भाला दिखाई दिया, \q इस्राएल के चालीस हज़ार में?
hi.B: इस्राएल ने नए देवता चुने; \q तब युद्ध नगर के फाटकों तक आ पहुँचा। \q न कोई ढाल दिखती थी, न भाला, \q इस्राएल के चालीस हज़ार में।
hi.R: इस्राएल ने नए देवताओं की पूजा करना चुना, \q और तब युद्ध ठीक नगर के फाटकों तक आ पहुँचा। \q एक भी ढाल या भाला नहीं मिलता था \q इस्राएल के चालीस हज़ार लोगों में।

ru.L: Избрал [Израиль] новых богов — \q тогда война [была у] ворот. \q Был ли виден щит или копьё \q у сорока тысяч в Израиле?
ru.B: Израиль избрал новых богов — \q и тогда война пришла к воротам городов. \q Не видно было ни щита, ни копья \q у сорока тысяч в Израиле.
ru.R: Израиль решил поклоняться новым богам, \q и тогда война подошла к самым воротам городов. \q Ни одного щита или копья не нашлось \q у сорока тысяч человек в Израиле.

ja.L: [イスラエルは]新しい神々を選んだ。 \q そのとき、戦いが門にあった。 \q 盾が見られただろうか、槍が、 \q イスラエルの四万人の中に？
ja.B: イスラエルは新しい神々を選んだ。 \q すると、戦いが町の門にまで及んだ。 \q 盾も槍も見当たらなかった。 \q イスラエルの四万人の中に。
ja.R: イスラエルは新しい神々を拝むことにした。 \q すると、戦いが町の門のすぐそばまでやって来た。 \q 盾も槍も一つも見つからなかった。 \q イスラエルの四万人の中に。

uk.L: [Ізраїль] обрав нових богів; \q тоді війна [була біля] брам. \q Чи видно було щит або спис \q серед сорока тисяч в Ізраїлі?
uk.B: Ізраїль обрав нових богів; \q тоді війна підступила до міських брам. \q Не видно було ні щита, ні списа \q серед сорока тисяч в Ізраїлі.
uk.R: Ізраїль вирішив поклонятися новим богам, \q і тоді війна підійшла до самих міських брам. \q Не можна було знайти жодного щита чи списа \q серед сорока тисяч в Ізраїлі.

id.L: [Israel] memilih allah-allah baru; \q lalu perang [ada di] pintu-pintu gerbang. \q Adakah terlihat perisai atau tombak \q di antara 40.000 orang di Israel?
id.B: Israel memilih allah-allah baru, \q lalu perang sampai di pintu-pintu gerbang. \q Tidak terlihat satu perisai atau tombak pun \q di antara 40.000 orang di Israel.
id.R: Israel memilih untuk menyembah dewa-dewa baru, \q lalu perang datang sampai ke pintu-pintu gerbang kota. \q Tidak ada satu perisai atau tombak pun \q di antara 40.000 orang di Israel.

zh.L: [以色列]选择了新的神明， \q 那时战争[就到了]城门。 \q 可曾看见一面盾牌、一支长矛， \q 在以色列的四万人中吗？
zh.B: 以色列选择了新的神明， \q 战火随即烧到城门。 \q 在以色列四万人中， \q 连一面盾牌、一支长矛也看不见。
zh.R: 以色列人选择去拜新的神明， \q 于是战争一直打到城门口。 \q 在以色列四万人中， \q 连一面盾牌、一支长矛也找不到。

pa.L: [ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਨੇ] ਨਵੇਂ ਦੇਵਤੇ ਚੁਣੇ; \q ਤਦ ਫਾਟਕਾਂ [ਉੱਤੇ] ਯੁੱਧ [ਸੀ]। \q ਕੀ ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਚਾਲੀ ਹਜ਼ਾਰਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ \q ਕੋਈ ਢਾਲ ਜਾਂ ਬਰਛਾ ਵਿਖਾਈ ਦਿੱਤਾ?
pa.B: ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਨੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਦੇਵਤੇ ਚੁਣ ਲਏ; \q ਤਦ ਯੁੱਧ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਦੇ ਫਾਟਕਾਂ ਤੱਕ ਆ ਪਹੁੰਚਿਆ। \q ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਚਾਲੀ ਹਜ਼ਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ \q ਇੱਕ ਢਾਲ ਜਾਂ ਬਰਛਾ ਵੀ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਸੀ।
pa.R: ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਨੇ ਨਵੇਂ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਪੂਜਾ ਕਰਨੀ ਚੁਣੀ, \q ਅਤੇ ਫਿਰ ਲੜਾਈ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਦੇ ਫਾਟਕਾਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਆ ਗਈ। \q ਇਸਰਾਏਲ ਦੇ ਚਾਲੀ ਹਜ਼ਾਰ ਆਦਮੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ \q ਇੱਕ ਵੀ ਢਾਲ ਜਾਂ ਬਰਛਾ ਲੱਭਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੀ।

tl.L: [Ang Israel] ay pumili ng mga bagong diyos; \q kaya ang digmaan [ay nasa] mga pintuang-bayan. \q May nakita bang kalasag, o sibat, \q sa apatnapung libo sa Israel?
tl.B: Pumili ang Israel ng mga bagong diyos; \q kaya dumating ang digmaan sa mga pintuang-bayan. \q Walang kalasag o sibat na makikita \q sa apatnapung libo sa Israel.
tl.R: Pinili ng Israel na sumamba sa mga bagong diyos, \q at pagkatapos ay umabot ang digmaan hanggang sa mga pintuang-bayan. \q Wala ni isang kalasag o sibat na matagpuan \q sa apatnapung libo sa Israel.

decisions.choice: Israel chose new gods: the people turned to other gods, and war followed
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, with Israel (or each one) as its subject. The book says again and again that Israel turned to other gods and was then handed over to its enemies (2:11-14; 4:1-2), and Deuteronomy 32:17 speaks of "new gods". The line is very hard, and the ancient translations differ. Others read "God chose new leaders" or "when they chose new gods".

decisions.choice: war at the gates: the enemy fought right at the gates of Israel's towns
alternatives: then there was fighting in the gates
decisions.reason: The word for "war" is found only here and seems to mean fighting. The gates were where a town was defended. Some divide or change the letters to get other sense, such as "barley bread".

decisions.choice: "was a shield seen?": not one shield or spear was to be seen
decisions.reason: The words "if it was seen" have the force of a strong denial. Israel had no weapons to fight with, as later under the Philistines (1 Samuel 13:19-22).

decisions.choice: forty thousand
decisions.reason: On the size of numbers counted in "thousands", see the note at Numbers 1.

decisions.choice: Israel
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; Israel is the people the song speaks of.

decisions.choice: the last two lines in Chinese order
decisions.reason: Chinese puts the place, "among forty thousand in Israel", before what is not seen, so Balanced and Readable swap the content of the last two lines; Literal keeps the Hebrew order with the question closed by 吗.

decisions.choice: "pumili ng mga bagong diyos"
decisions.reason: The people turned to other gods, and war followed (m1).

decisions.choice: "ang digmaan ay nasa mga pintuang-bayan"
decisions.reason: The enemy fought right at the gates of Israel's towns (m2).

decisions.choice: "May nakita bang kalasag?"
decisions.reason: Not one shield or spear was to be seen (m3).

decisions.choice: "apatnapung libo"
decisions.reason: Forty thousand (m4).

source.text: לִבִּי֙ לְחוֹקְקֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַמִּֽתְנַדְּבִ֖ים בָּעָ֑ם בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: My heart [is] to [the] commanders of Israel, the ones offering themselves willingly among the people; bless Yahweh!

en.L: My heart [is] toward the commanders of Israel, \q those offering themselves willingly among the people. \q Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.B: My heart is with the commanders of Israel, \q who volunteered freely among the people. \q Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.R: My heart is with Israel's commanders, \q who gladly came forward from among the people. \q Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

sw.L: Moyo wangu [uko] kwa majemadari wa Israeli, \q wale waliojitoa kwa hiari kati ya watu. \q Mhimidini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.B: Moyo wangu uko pamoja na majemadari wa Israeli, \q waliojitolea kwa hiari kati ya watu. \q Mhimidini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.R: Moyo wangu uko pamoja na majemadari wa Israeli, \q waliojitokeza kwa furaha kutoka kati ya watu. \q Msifuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!

es.L: Mi corazón [está] con los jefes de Israel, \q los que se ofrecieron voluntariamente entre el pueblo. \q ¡{{plural_you:Bendigan|Bendecid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!
es.B: Mi corazón está con los jefes de Israel, \q que se ofrecieron de buena gana entre el pueblo. \q ¡{{plural_you:Bendigan|Bendecid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!
es.R: Mi corazón está con los jefes de Israel, \q que se presentaron con gusto de entre el pueblo. \q ¡{{plural_you:Alaben|Alabad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}!

fr.L: Mon cœur [va] vers les chefs d’Israël, \q ceux qui s’offrent de plein gré parmi le peuple. \q Bénissez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !
fr.B: Mon cœur est avec les chefs d’Israël, \q qui se sont engagés librement parmi le peuple. \q Bénissez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !
fr.R: Mon cœur est avec les chefs d’Israël, \q qui se sont présentés de bon cœur du milieu du peuple. \q Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} !

vi.L: Lòng tôi [hướng về] các vị chỉ huy của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q những người tự nguyện dâng mình giữa dân chúng. \q Hãy chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!
vi.B: Lòng tôi ở cùng các vị chỉ huy của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q là những người đã tự nguyện ra đi giữa dân chúng. \q Hãy chúc tụng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!
vi.R: Lòng tôi ở cùng các vị chỉ huy của Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q là những người đã vui lòng đứng ra từ giữa dân chúng. \q Hãy ca ngợi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!

ko.L: 내 마음이 이스라엘의 지휘관들을 [향한다]. \q 백성 가운데 스스로 기꺼이 나선 사람들을. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!
ko.B: 내 마음은 이스라엘의 지휘관들과 함께 있다. \q 그들은 백성 가운데서 기꺼이 자원하여 나섰다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!
ko.R: 내 마음은 이스라엘의 지휘관들과 함께 있다. \q 그들은 백성 가운데서 기쁘게 앞으로 나섰다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 찬양하여라!

pt.L: O meu coração [está] com os comandantes de Israel, \q os que se ofereceram de boa vontade entre o povo. \q Bendigam {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!
pt.B: O meu coração está com os comandantes de Israel, \q que se apresentaram como voluntários entre o povo. \q Bendigam {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!
pt.R: O meu coração está com os comandantes de Israel, \q que se ofereceram com alegria do meio do povo. \q Louvem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}!

am.L: ልቤ ወደ እስራኤል አዛዦች [ነው]፤ \q በሕዝቡ መካከል ራሳቸውን በፈቃዳቸው ወዳቀረቡት። \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ባርኩ!
